applies_why: The judge text resolves a collision between Romans 1:3 descent according to the flesh and the Holy Ghost conception by treating it as underdetermined for lack of explicit textual resolution, so it does the chain-assessment K-C governs.
quote: D6 vs C4 (Romans 1:3): UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] section A.1-2 and [CR3] Link 6 premises 1-3, where descent according to the flesh is weighed against conception of the Holy Ghost without explicit textual resolution of paternity.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: states the contrary in its own words: one reading limits this to rejecting a link solely because no single verse states the contrary; the other also bars demanding explicit textual resolution for the chain. I used the broader reading.
why: The judge treats the absence of an explicit textual resolution of paternity as decisive, which is the retired stating-verse approach rather than weighing the parties' chains by footing as K-C requires.
